name: veewee/xml
input_api: VeeWee\Xml\Encoding\xml_decode(string $xml, callable ...$configurators): array, documented as "Decodes an XML string into an array". It loads the text with Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString($xml, 0) inside disallow_issues (any libxml error or warning throws, wrapped as EncodingException) and converts the document element into veewee's PHP array format. The same loader backs Dom\Document::fromXmlString; Dom\Document::fromXmlFile and Reader::fromXmlFile/fromXmlString (XMLReader) are the documented file and streaming entry points
parser_family: libxml2 via PHP ext/dom Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString; shared with the standard DOMDocument path, sabre/xml (XMLReader), symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer
package_own_scope: Encoding\Internal\Decoder: the DOM-to-array mapping (qualified element names as keys, same-named siblings grouped into lists, '@attributes' with qualified names, '@namespaces' with each element's own xmlns declarations, '@value' for text next to attributes, leaf text via textContent) plus the Dom\Document string loader and libxml issue collection. Tokenizing, well-formedness, entity and CDATA decoding and namespace binding are libxml2; turning xmlns declarations into attributes is PHP ext/dom.
family: libxml2 via PHP Dom\XMLDocument, shared with the standard path, sabre/xml, symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer

popularity.caveat: Cumulative downloads of the whole veewee/xml package (rank 13 in the snapshot's 'xml' query, 3 in 'xml reader', 4 in 'xml decoder'). They are a package adoption proxy, not xml_decode uses: the package also covers DOM manipulation, XMLReader streaming, XMLWriter, XSD and XSLT, and many installs come through dependents such as php-soap and saloonphp/xml-wrangler. It shares the libxml2 parser family with the standard path, sabre/xml, symfony/dom-crawler and symfony/serializer.

caveats: xml_decode keys elements and attributes by qualified name (prefix:local) and lists each element's own xmlns declarations under '@namespaces' ('' for the default namespace), including the order control's nested <plain xmlns=""> undeclaration. It does not report namespace URIs per element, so the summary keeps qualified names plus indexed per-element declarations and the oracle parses without namespace processing; resolving the summary's names through its declarations reproduces expat's namespace-aware expanded names on both controls, so no namespace information is lost on them.

Information xml_decode drops by design: comments and processing instructions (the order control's top-level comment and <?audit?> PI), the CDATA/text distinction (note's CDATA comes back as plain 'x < y'), text of elements that also have child elements (whitespace-only in both controls; mixed-content text would be lost), and document order of non-adjacent same-named siblings, which are grouped into one list keyed by name (adjacent in both controls). All values are strings.

The harness calls xml_decode($bytes) with no configurators. Its loader runs Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString($xml, 0) inside disallow_issues, so any libxml error or warning raises EncodingException; it was run only on the two valid controls. The documented file and streaming APIs (Dom\Document::fromXmlFile, Reader::fromXmlFile/fromXmlString over XMLReader) were not exercised.

Xdebug covers 295 veewee/xml lines in 186 files on both controls, with identical line sets: 161 of them are single declaration lines of function files that src/bootstrap.php loads for every use, and 77 are in Encoding/ (14 in the Decoder\Builder\element.php builder). Both controls take the same decoder branches, so veewee/xml's own lines do not distinguish them.

AFL++ feedback is not package-own: the native overlay runs the same xml_decode harness on PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4 with only libxml2 parser.c, parserInternals.c, SAX2.c and PHP ext/dom/xml_document.c and document.c instrumented. The 361 tuples that differ between the controls all also differ under a bare Dom\XMLDocument::createFromString, and the 2 post-parse tuples are the same for both controls. ext/dom/namespace_compat.c was tried and left out: with it the maps held 1149/1273 tuples and one differing tuple appeared only when veewee's attribute traversal ran.
